title: Corrosion — tailgate at the wing mounts
blurb: Rust around where the GT wing bolts through the tailgate skin. This one has an obvious cause and an obvious lesson.
symptom: Corrosion breaking out around the wing's mounting points on the tailgate.
cause:
Every hole drilled through a painted steel panel exposes bare edge metal. Unless that edge is sealed on both faces, water wicks in around the fastener, sits between the wing foot and the paint, and corrodes outward from the hole. A rubber gasket under the wing foot holds the water in rather than keeping it out.

This was predictable, and it is on the mods page

The GT wing dossier already flags it: "Every new hole through the tailgate skin is a corrosion start point. Seal both faces and cavity-wax the inside." That is what has happened. The same warning applies to the tail bar project, which cuts a 1.1 metre aperture in the same panel — worth getting the method right on this repair first.

check.t: Remove the wing and look at the panel underneath
check.hint: The visible rust is the edge of it, not the whole of it.

check.t: Check inside the tailgate around each hole
check.hint: Trim board off. Corrosion from a drilled hole works both ways.

check.t: Check the tailgate drain paths are clear
Look at the glass flange and the lower edge while it is apart
Decide whether the wing goes back on the same holes
check.hint: Repairing around existing holes is harder than filling them and starting again.

fix:
1. Wing off, panel cleaned back to bright metal around every hole.
  2. Treat, etch prime, and — the step that gets skipped — seal the bare edge inside each hole, not just the visible face.
  3. Colour and lacquer, then cavity-wax the inside of the tailgate.
  4. Refit on new fasteners with a sealant bead under each foot, not a bare rubber pad.

Added mass high on the tailgate also works the gas struts harder — worth checking they still hold the panel up while it is all apart.
